verdict: The updated studio resolves the demonstrated focus/viewport failure and makes comparison possible beside the performance. The independent pointer-to-keyboard challenge exposed a partial fix, which was corrected and retested. Final keyboard-ring evidence resolves the capture ambiguity. No remaining interaction blocker is reproduced within this local review's scope.
resolvedIssues: Observed: keyboard activation of Angry now focuses the player heading at viewport y=25.3. The next Tab reaches the visible Both radio without leaving scrollY229. This replaces the previous jump to the offscreen Disgusted card and consequent interruption of the performance.

Observed: the first implementation exempted pointer clicks from focus transfer. The requested mixed-input check reproduced the old failure: clicking Angry then pressing Tab returned to Disgusted at scrollY1866.5. Final evidence records pointer activation focusing the same heading and subsequent Tab staying at scrollY229. The correction addresses navigation intent consistently across these tested inputs.

Observed in source and screenshots: the new Feeling selector has an associated label and native grouped options; adjacent buttons have explicit Previous feeling and Next feeling names. Captured wraparound reaches Disgusted from the beginning and Curious from the end while retaining focus on the initiating button. These local controls reduce repeated trips through the long gallery without removing any emotions.

Observed: automatic collection advance keeps focus on sequence, rather than repeatedly moving it to changing headings. Manual selection cancels the collection. Pause, resume and rest remain functional in captured engine states. Source places focus transfer only inside intentional gallery activation, not inside the shared choose function.

Observed: reduced-motion selection shows Excited at its held pose, with playing=false and collection disabled. Home and End on the timeline reach time zero and duration without starting playback. Source also removes active-button translation under reduced motion; the full gallery and selector remain available.

Source observation: the status now includes the selected emotion and uses an atomic polite announcement. Text is changed only when that status differs, preserving protection against animation-frame chatter. The heading's described position supplies context such as Feeling 23 of 24. Actual spoken output has not been heard.

Observed: the final genuine keyboard activation capture shows a visible heading ring. interaction-extra.json confirms :focus-visible=true and a solid 3px outline; the earlier ringless capture did not establish a defect. Measurements at 1440, 1024, 768, 390 and 320 CSS pixels show no horizontal document overflow. This demonstrates the checked geometry, not every possible text or assistive setting.
limits: Independent review of current source, before snapshots and fresh root-captured evidence; no peer opinions consulted, browser operated or production files edited by this specialist.

The native selector probe retained focus but Home, ArrowDown and Enter did not change Angry. Do not count that probe as successful keyboard selection. Programmatic selection and source handlers were validated; physical native-selection, screen-reader and real touch-device behavior remain unproven. This limitation is not evidence that the native control is broken.

No conformance certification, full assistive-technology traversal, forced-colors or zoom audit. Conclusions apply to this local interactive studio, not future-site architecture, static GitHub readiness or audience appeal.
